evidence.observation: At 14:09:41Z checkout submit_order failed with HTTP 401 from payment-api; at 14:10:03Z the checkout flow was still blocked by payment authentication failure.
At 14:08:59Z payment authentication failed through auth-gateway because issuer partner-v2 was not allowed; create_payment was rejected at 14:09:04Z.
AUTH-2026-0318 was deployed at 14:05:12Z, changing the JWKS namespace and issuer to partner-v2; validation then failed because allowed_issuers still contained partner-v1.
At 14:10Z checkout-web, payment-api, and auth-gateway had elevated HTTP 401 rates of 18.7%, 21.2%, and 28.4%, respectively, while checkout and payment latency also rose.
The dependency path is checkout-web -> payment-api -> auth-gateway, and AUTH-2026-0318 is the recent change on auth-gateway closest to the incident.

excluded_red_herrings.why_not_primary: The database log reports normal 35 ms query latency, zero errors, and no failed checkout transaction reached orders-db before the auth gate.
The metric note isolates the failures to images, and checkout-web reports static assets served normally after retry while checkout submissions remained blocked.
Topology and logs place the failing request on the payment/auth branch; the database change was vacuum tuning only, with no schema or credential change.

recommended_next_steps: Immediately pause or roll back AUTH-2026-0318, or add partner-v2 to auth-gateway allowed_issuers after validating the intended issuer configuration.
Refresh or invalidate the affected JWKS cache namespace and confirm partner-v2 keys are retrievable without fallback to partner-v1.
Run a controlled checkout payment-authentication test and verify auth-gateway, payment-api, and checkout-web HTTP 401 rates and p95 latency return to baseline.
Review the change validation and rollout guardrails so issuer and allowed_issuers cannot diverge in a production deployment.
